column1: # Tab-separated. Read by EvalCorpusTest. THIS FILE MUST STAY UTF-8 (no BOM) --
# the expected outputs contain U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT and the loader rejects U+FFFD.
# Columns (exactly 6, tab-separated, no tabs inside a field):
#   id             stable row id. Never renumber a live row; append new ids.
#   input          the text handed to the parser. Escapes: \t \n \r \\ \uXXXX
#                  (astral chars are written as a UTF-16 surrogate pair, e.g.
#                  \uD83C\uDF89 = U+1F389. Leading/trailing spaces of a field
#                  are written \u0020 so editors cannot silently eat them.)
#   expect_detect  yes | no -- what TimeParser.detect(input).isNotEmpty() SHOULD return
#   expect_output  the exact full string TimeConverter.splice SHOULD return,
#                  or the literal token  =input  when nothing should change
#   category       see below -- decides whether the row can fail the build
#   note           free text; for ambiguous/unverified rows this carries the reasoning
#     must_detect      happy paths, alias coverage, formatting
#     unicode          emoji / RTL / non-Latin splice-index behaviour
#     idempotent       a second pass must not change the text again
#   reporting only (printed, never fails the build):
#     known_gap        DESIRED behaviour that the code does not yet produce.
#                      These are real defects, encoded so the score shows them.
#     ambiguous        the right answer is genuinely debatable. expect_output is
#                      a PROPOSAL for the owner to adjudicate; note says why.
#     unverified       expected value derived by reading the source but not yet
#                      confirmed against a real JVM run. Promote or fix after
#   Every row is pinned by the harness, never by wall-clock time:
#                     Europe/London  -> rendered as CT, ET, PT, UK in that order
#     system default  pinned to America/New_York for the duration of the class
#   Rows that depend on the fixed clock (they would drift with a real clock):
#     - EVERY row whose expect_output contains a rendered stamp. The rendered
#       times themselves are clock-independent, but the UTC offsets used to
#       compute them are date-dependent (2026-05-18 = US DST on, UK BST on,
#       AU/NZ DST off). Change NOW and most expect_output values change.
#   Rows that additionally depend on the pinned SYSTEM DEFAULT zone (they have
#   no explicit zone token, so the parser falls back to ZoneId.systemDefault()):
#   If the pin is removed these become machine-dependent -- that fallback is the
# ADDING A ROW: see README.md in this directory.
